correctness.rationale: For arbitrary Hilbert images \(A_i,B_i\), two directly expanded squared-norm identities imply sharp lower bounds \(4(n-1)/(n-1+r)\), \(4(n-2)/n\), and \(r(n-2)/(2(n-1))\), where \(r=s^2\). Their maximum has exactly the stated thresholds for \(n\ge3\) and \(1\le r\le9\). Two orthogonal centered regular simplices attain the low branch; one antipodal regular simplex attains plateau and high branch with precise scaling. Saturated distance-class averages and equality in the two identities fix every pairwise distance of every optimum. Gram uniqueness gives exact affine dimensions \(2n-2\) below the first transition and \(n-1\) at and above it. The proof verifies all parameters analytically; exact rational tests cover 161 witnesses and 120 independent arbitrary-vector Hilbert-identity cases. Finite tests do not certify infinitely many cases.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic SDP characterizations are not an evaluated closed classification, and general graph spectral bounds do not identify all sharp embeddings at interior non-distance-regular weighted s. The \(s=1\)/\(s=3\) corollaries are subsumed by published work and excluded from priority claim; the interior 3-branch exact curve and rigidity are additional statements requiring the two new equality identities and constructions.

originality.rationale: Claims concern the continuous interior matching-stretch family, exact three-branch least Hilbert distortion, constant plateau, all-extremizer rigidity and affine-rank jump. Published results for the unstretched complete bipartite endpoint \(s=1\) and unweighted crown endpoint \(s=3\) are expressly acknowledged as prior. Full primary papers on distortion, spectral graph bounds and distorted negative type were inspected for dominating claims; no interior evaluated classification was located. A general semidefinite dual characterization is a method, not an explicit evaluation of this phase law. Unindexed equivalent literature remains possible.

value.rationale: The one-orbit matching-edge deformation continuously joins two canonical graph metrics. The exact Hilbert distortion measures Euclidean representation cost; the open flat phase and simultaneous collapse of minimum optimal affine dimension from \(2n-2\) to \(n-1\) are nonroutine structural behavior, throughout an infinite metric family. The equality classification describes all optimizers, not merely a value or one example.
